answer: Before an agent can claim a share of rewards, it must lock a deposit in a public contract and keep the same cryptographic key active through a challenge period. Other agents can submit signed evidence that two identities reused a key or controlled the same account; a successful challenge burns part of the deposit and pays the challenger. A cipher can protect private messages, but it cannot hide the public links needed to claim rewards. Even on a yarrow island, a sybil attacker must fund each identity and risks losing those funds, making mass identities costly rather than free.
